<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **20** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-provider-lifecycle.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-provider-lifecycle.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `31df31070eeca247f46eac046389651e94286e85` — the merge of head `c4c70109fe8bb983548a263606745059a1c44de9` into base `25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 31df31070eeca247f46eac046389651e94286e85 && git checkout 31df31070eeca247f46eac046389651e94286e85
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f c4c70109fe8bb983548a263606745059a1c44de9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f && git merge --no-ff c4c70109fe8bb983548a263606745059a1c44de9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 25ee507651f7bae209771fb31661e6edf46f4c8f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Read: the PR body, its 5 comments, its 10-file list, the net diff against `main`, the 57 check-runs on this head (40 success, 17 skipped, 0 failed), the readings at this head and the open-choice options. Cited code read and not reviewed: `audience-posture.ts`, `sso-sign-in-options.ts`, `objectql-adapter.ts`, `auth-manager-before-hook.ts`, `register-sso-provider.ts`, `scim-sso-adoption.ts`, `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-sso-provider.object.ts`, `packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts`, and the installed `@better-auth/sso`, `better-auth`, `@better-auth/core` 1.7.12 and `tldts-core` 7.4.16.

### ① Derived judgments

Each change the diff implies, named right or wrong.

1. Account creation, verification on: a new account through a SAML or OIDC provider is admitted only when the address's domain equals a domain the provider lists and has verified. The accept set narrows. **Right**: it is the declared `(narrowing)`, behind a switch that is off by default.
2. The address: its domain part, after the last `@`, must already be a bare host in its one spelling; case, and the Unicode and punycode forms of one name, are one domain. **Right**: an allowlist and then equality, so each check can refuse more and never admit more.
3. The entry: for this rule a stored `domain` entry counts only when it is written as a bare host, one trailing root dot allowed. That is narrower than the vendor's own parse of the same entry. **Right** under option B, judged in ③.
4. The wire: no error code is added. `EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED` gains a second producer, the SSO callback under every audience posture, and it is answered ahead of the audience gate, so where both rules refuse, this code is the one sent. **Right**: plugin-auth's ledger set is unchanged, and the first answer is the one no invitation lifts. Nit N3 is about the code's recorded meaning.
5. The package's public surface: nothing is added. The new module is not exported from the entry, `AuthInstanceHost` (one new member) is internal, and `AuthManager.isSsoDomainVerificationEnabled` keeps its signature. **Right**.
6. The authorable surface: `AuthPluginConfig.ssoDomainVerification` keeps its key, type, default and description, and no authorable-surface shard moves. **Right**.
7. Data at rest: no column, no row shape, nothing rewritten. **Right**.
8. Outside the rule and unchanged: verification off; accounts that exist; linking; creations whose source is `method: 'oauth'`; SCIM. **Right** as the declared scope; ③ carries what is escalated about it.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`, a `!` summary, a BREAKING paragraph with Who moves, the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, and both declarations, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, each at the start of a line in the PR body and in the changeset body.

It matches what the diff publishes. One package publishes. No authorable key, accepted value or default moves, so the kind is `none` and the level is `patch`; a narrowing keeps its BREAKING carriers at `patch`. Considered and not owed: `semantic`. The published meaning of `ssoDomainVerification` (DNS domain verification for SSO providers) stands, and the diff completes what that verification enforces. `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head, 2 runs of 2. **Right**.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and open question, answered or escalated.

- **Open question, A or B, with C as a follow-up: B, and file C.** B depends on no parser: an entry made only of letters, marks, digits, `.` and `-` has one reading under every host parser, so the host the flag was set for is the host the rule reads, whatever vendor version ran the proof. A has plugin-auth re-run a vendor function that is not exported, through a dependency it would declare itself (the vendor's range is `^7.4.3`, the lockfile resolves 7.4.16), and take the agreement of two parsers today as the proof made when the flag was set. That coupling has to be kept in step at every vendor bump, for a spelling the vendor's own TODO retires and that the platform's form, docs and examples never taught. B's cost is stated in Who moves. C is owed, not optional: with B alone an entry in another spelling is stored and verified and then counts for nothing, and only the docs say why. A refusal at the write door tells the author there, and it leaves one stored spelling that the claim rule, the SCIM adoption rule and this rule all read alike.
- Deviation, two PRs for one order: right for the tiers. The order of the two landings is judged on #32638's record.
- Deviation, no declaration lines on the ADR PR: answered on #32638's record.
- Deviation, a temporary probe test run and removed: the file list is 10 paths, none stray.
- Rework round, NOT MEASURED (full suite, gates, dogfood, CI): answered by the readings at this head. Package suite 265 files, 4938 tests passed, 10 skipped. Typecheck exit 0. The 3 touched files 151 passed. Gates 105 derived, 104 exit 0, 1 not measured locally (its prerequisite build), and `Build Core`, the CI job that hosts it, concluded success. Dogfood 452 files passed, 3 skipped. Check-runs as counted above.
- Rework round, stale PR body: the body now states the entry rule and the 151. The tree is what was judged.
- Out of scope, the SCIM adoption rule's own parse of the same list: a valid consistency finding, not this diff's. A follow-up card; C serves it too.
- Docs-drift advisory (3 pages name `AuthManager`; `sso-provider-lifecycle.ts` yielded no anchor): the 3 pages carry 0 sentences about domain verification or SSO account creation, so none needs an edit. The uncovered hunk is one comment paragraph, and the page that states the rule is in this diff.
- `security_findings: withheld`, 2 reports, and the items the rework report lists as untouched: with the owner seat, not read here.
- For the lane seat's ACCEPT of the changeset, which is not reviewed here: Who moves, first bullet, tells a deployment to list and verify each other domain. Only a domain's owner can do that. The bullet has no line for an address at a domain the deployment cannot prove.
- **Escalated to the seat, contract authority.** The diff settles a contract point: no posture, invitation, JIT toggle or first-human carve-out relaxes the rule, so with verification on, an invited address at a domain the provider has not proven gets no account through SSO.
